title: Elder Souls Quest Definition
description: Canonical serialisation for every quest in the game. Load-bearing: all quest-side critic metrics (branch count, solution count, failure states, non-combat resolvability, deceit coverage, unique-reward fraction, faction escalation shape) are computed by static analysis over files validating against this schema. A quest that cannot be expressed here is a quest that cannot be judged, and is therefore out of spec.

id.description: Stable quest id, e.g. Q-HIST-04, Q-MAIN-11, Q-SIDE-063.

category.description: hidden = never offered by a giver; must be discovered from world state, a book, or overheard dialogue.

faction.description: Faction id this quest belongs to, or null for main/side.

act.description: Main-quest act number (see RI-QST06). Null for non-main quests.

rank_gate.description: Rank the player must already hold to be offered this quest. Never a character-level gate — see RI-QST03.

discovery.description: given = a giver offers it via a topic. overheard = surfaced only by a rumour/topic on an unrelated NPC. found = a book, note, corpse, or ledger. environmental = the world state itself is the prompt. consequence = opened by the outcome of another quest.

honest.description: false when the giver's stated objective differs from their actual objective. If false, `deceit` MUST be present.

topic.description: The dialogue topic keyword that opens this quest. No quest is opened by a map marker.

overheard_from.description: NPC ids whose rumour text seeds the topic. Required when discovery == overheard.

stakes.description: Personal stake for the player character. 1 = a stranger's errand. 10 = the player's own standing, life, or the world.

directions.description: Prose wayfinding as spoken by the giver. Must be sufficient to reach the target without a marker. Landmarks, directions, distances in walking terms.

journal.description: Numbered, non-contiguous journal indices in Morrowind style. Text is first-person, authored by the player character, and may record the player's mistaken belief.

records_belief.description: true when this entry states something the player believes but which the quest later contradicts. This is the journal-as-unreliable-narrator flag.

branches.description: Points where player choice or discovered information forks the quest. A quest with zero branches is a chore.

condition.description: Human-readable predicate: what the player learns, chooses, or fails.

items.description: id of a resolution, a failure_state, a sibling branch, or a deceit.revealed_by entry. Every target must resolve within this file.

resolutions.description: Every distinct way the quest can end in a non-failure state.

skills.description: Keys must be skill ids from game/data/progression/skills.json. gate.js canResolve() looks the key up VERBATIM in sim.progression.skills, so a key that is not in the register reports `0/N` for as long as the game runs and no amount of play can move it. Note the two adjacent registers one underscore apart: `root-speech` is the SKILL, `root_speech` is the SCHOOL in game/data/magic/effects.json. Checked by tools/quests/attr-scale-audit.mjs; warned by tools/check-quests.mjs.

attributes.description: Attribute demands are declared on the DERIVED scale, NOT Morrowind's 0-100 one. An attribute is worth `creation value + 6 per skill that governs it` and no more: character/derive.js grants +1 per multiple of 15 crossed in a governing skill, and the bought stream in engine.js _spendSouls() has no funding source because nothing in the build awards souls. Measured over 240 signatures (reports/faction-signature-sweep.json) personality tops out at 18/22/31 on a p10/median/best sheet, so `personality: 40` is not a hard check - it is unreachable by every character the game can create. Set a demand from the measured ceiling WITH RESERVE, at or under `median ceiling - 2`; clamping to the ceiling itself is the same defect one point lower and shut Act IV for 11 of 40 signatures. Checked by tools/quests/attr-scale-audit.mjs; warned by tools/check-quests.mjs.

knowledge.description: Topic ids or book ids the player must have actually read/heard. Lore as a key.

violence_required.description: true if reaching this resolution requires killing at least one living NPC or creature. Drives the non-combat resolution metric (RI-QST05).

outcome.description: What actually happens in the world.

morally_better.description: null when the quest genuinely does not adjudicate. Overuse of true/false is a design smell.

requires_knowing.description: Deceit-truth ids (from deceit.revealed_by) that must have been discovered for this resolution to be available at all. This is the mechanism by which talking to the target before killing them opens a door.

consequences.description: What THIS ending does, on top of the quest-level `consequences` that every ending does. ADDED wave 1 by W1-18 as AM-QST04-W1-18-01: RI-QST09 X7 requires each exclusive pair to differ by >= 3 world_flags, a reward and >= 1 world entity, and with consequences declared only at quest level two exclusive resolutions of the same quest are IDENTICAL in the data by construction, so X7 is unmeasurable and fails closed. Purely additive - `resolutions[]` is additionalProperties:false, so every existing quest file still validates unchanged.

failure_states.description: Ways the quest ends without resolution. An empty array is legal only when `can_fail` is explicitly false, and that must be rare.

silent.description: true when the game never tells the player they failed; the journal simply stops. Powerful, use sparingly.

before_point_of_no_return.description: true if this reveal is reachable while the player can still act on it. At least one reveal per deceitful quest MUST be true.

journal.description: OPTIONAL. The journal index the player writes when they learn this truth, i.e. the entry that IS this reveal in prose. ADDED wave 1 by W1-18 round 2 as AM-QST04-W1-18-02. QuestEngine.note() -- the verb that writes the MIDDLE of a journal -- had exactly one caller in game/src/ (the hooks.json journal branch, covering 11 of 120 quests), so for 109 quests nothing a player does could write an entry between opening and closing. A reveal learned in the world is the commonest reason a player writes something down, and the entry is usually ALREADY AUTHORED and unreachable: Q-MAIN-06's journal 40 IS rev_the_curve_predates and 55 IS rev_the_steward_named. Must name a non-terminal ('active' or 'branch') entry of the same quest -- note() refuses 'success'/'failure' -- and is checked by tools/check-quests.mjs. Purely additive: a row without it reveals and writes nothing, exactly as before.

never_revealed.description: true for lies the player may never uncover. Capped by RI-QST02 scoring.

kill_required_npcs.description: NPCs/creatures that MUST die on every path. Empty array = quest is zero-kill completable. This array is the ground truth for the RI-QST05 ratio.

unique_named.description: true only for a one-of-a-kind item, location, or standing that exists nowhere else in the game and is named in fiction.

on_resolution.description: Resolution ids that grant this reward. Omitted = all resolutions.

faction_reputation.description: Signed reputation delta per faction id. Deltas for OTHER factions are how questlines contradict each other.

locks.description: Quest or faction ids permanently closed by completing this quest.
